PointFetchOk.doc: Result of a successful predicate-pushdown match. Carries the same shape as the standard CompileSelectOk plus the (constant) num_aggregates = 0 — lifted into its own type so the call site at /parts/compiler/parts/select-compile reads as a discriminated short-circuit (`Some(point_fetch) | None → fall through`). Field semantics match CompileSelectOk; opcode_template_kind is the integer index into the rule registry (v1: only one rule, RowidPointFetch = 0) used for telemetry / debug prints.

PushdownTrigger.doc: Closed enumeration of recognised push-down rules. v1 admits exactly one variant (RowidPointFetch); the variant exists as a placeholder for follow-ups that add additional rules (for example, range scans against an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY using <=, >=, BETWEEN; or unique-index point fetches once /parts/storage/parts/index lands).

RowidPointFetch.doc: WHERE clause is exactly `pk_col = expr` or `expr = pk_col` against an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY column, expr is row-independent, and the SELECT carries no DISTINCT / ORDER BY / LIMIT / OFFSET / GROUP BY / HAVING / compound. Lowers to OpenRead + key-expr compile + SeekRowid (miss → end) + Column reads + ResultRow + Close + Halt.

EmitOp.doc: A symbolic step in the v1 RowidPointFetch emit template. Generators consume this list in order to render the target-specific opcode sequence. The template is independent of label numbering — generators allocate fresh PC labels for `MissLabel` and `HaltLabel` and resolve them in a two-pass walk over the emitted opcode list. KeyExprCompile is a placeholder for the spliced output of the imported expr-compile call against the key_expr captured at recognition time.

KeyExprCompile.doc: Splice in the opcode sequence produced by compile_expr against the recognised key_expr; result lands in reg_key (= ncol).

SeekRowidByKey.doc: Emit SeekRowid { cursor: 0, rowid_reg: reg_key, jump_if_miss: MissLabel }.

ColumnReadAll.doc: For each column c in schema.columns, emit Column { cursor: 0, col_idx: c.index, dest_reg: c.index }.

ProjectionCompile.doc: Splice in the opcode sequence produced by expanding & compiling the projection list (Star / TableStar / Expr items) into contiguous registers starting at reg_key + 1. Records (proj_start, proj_count) for the trailing ResultRow.

EmitResultRow.doc: Emit ResultRow { start_reg: proj_start, count: proj_count }.

BindMissLabel.doc: Resolve MissLabel to the next PC. SeekRowid's miss-jump lands here.

CloseCursor.doc: Emit Close { cursor: 0 }. Idempotent. Emitted once on the hit path before the convergence point and once on the miss path; both lead into BindHaltLabel.

BindHaltLabel.doc: Resolve HaltLabel to the next PC.

RowidPointFetchTemplate.doc: The v1 emit-list template, recorded as data so the master.md prose and every target's mapping can cross-reference it. Generators MAY hard-code the equivalent emit sequence directly; this record exists to pin the canonical order. `steps` is the literal sequence that the emitter walks.

try_compile_point_fetch.doc: Recognise-and-emit. Returns Some(PointFetchOk) iff every Pin 1–6 in master.md holds for `stmt` against `schema`; returns None otherwise. None is the signal to /parts/compiler/parts/select-compile to fall through to its standard single-table emitter. The function MUST NOT mutate the schema or the stmt; it MUST NOT raise CompileError on a recogniser mismatch (mismatch is None, not an error). It MAY return Err only if the recogniser matches but the spliced compile_expr call against key_expr or the projection compile fails — that propagates through as a CompileError exactly as the standard emitter would.

find_rowid_index.doc: Helper: given a TableSchema, return the first IndexSpec whose kind is Rowid, or None. v1 mem-store guarantees at most one such entry per table. Made a public helper so /parts/compiler/parts/select-compile and follow-up rules can share the lookup. Implementations consult schema's installed indexes list — the wiring from TableSchema (compiler-side) to MemTable.indexes (storage-side) lives in the schema-install path of select-compile.

is_row_independent.doc: Helper: structural walk over `expr` returning true iff the AST contains zero Col references and zero Star / TableStar references and zero Subquery / Exists / InSubquery nodes. Bind parameters (Param), literals, Cast, Unary, Binary, and Call (whose args are themselves row-independent) are admitted. Public helper so follow-up rules can reuse the predicate.
